# Copilot instructions for rclone

rclone is a Go command-line program ("rsync for cloud storage") that syncs files
to and from 50+ cloud storage providers. Requires the Go version in `go.mod`
(currently go 1.25).

## Build, test, lint

- Build: `go build` (`make` adds an accurate version string) → `./rclone`.
- Quick unit tests (whole repo): `make quicktest` — runs
  `RCLONE_CONFIG="/notfound" go test ./...`. The bogus config path keeps tests
  from touching your real config.
- Race detector: `make racequicktest`.
- Single package: `cd backend/onedrive && go test -v`.
- Single test by name: `go test -v -run TestNameRegexp ./fs/operations/`.
- Lint (matches CI): `make check` — runs `golangci-lint run ./...` plus
  `bin/markdown-lint`. Config is `.golangci.yml` / `.markdownlint.yml`.
- Install golangci-lint at the pinned version with `make build_dep`.

## Backend integration tests

Most backend tests run against a real remote configured under a special name.
For backend `remote`, create a config remote named `TestRemote`, then:

```console
cd backend/remote && go test -v               # unit tests (skipped if TestRemote: undefined)
cd fs/operations && go test -v -remote TestRemote:
cd fs/sync      && go test -v -remote TestRemote: -fast-list
go run ./fstest/test_all -backends remote      # full framework with HTML report + retries
```

## Architecture (the big picture)

rclone is built around a small set of interfaces in `fs/types.go` (`Fs`,
`Object`, `Info`, optional feature interfaces). Everything is wired by blank
imports, not registries you edit by hand:

- `backend/` — one directory per cloud provider, each implementing the `fs`
  interfaces. `backend/all/all.go` blank-imports every backend; a new backend
  must be added there to be available.
- `cmd/` — one directory per CLI command. `cmd/all/all.go` blank-imports every
  command. Commands are built on cobra.
- `fs/` — the core, deliberately minimal. Key subpackages: `operations`
  (Copy/Move/etc. primitives), `sync` (directory sync), `config`, `filter`
  (include/exclude), `accounting` (stats + bandwidth limiting), `fshttp`
  (the shared HTTP transport), `walk`, `march`.
- `lib/` — shared helpers backends use: `rest` (REST/XML/JSON over net/http),
  `oauthutil` (OAuth), `dircache` (dir-ID caching), `pacer` (retry/backoff),
  `encoder` (path-name encoding).
- `vfs/` — virtual filesystem layer backing `mount`, `serve`, etc.
- `fstest/` — the integration test framework (`fstests` shared backend suite,
  `test_all` runner).
- `librclone/` — in-memory C/embedding API.

## Conventions

- **Keep backends uniform.** There are 50+ backends maintained in parallel.
  Copy an existing similar backend (box for directory-based, b2 for
  bucket-based) and follow its code order, function names, layout, and comments
  exactly. Don't rearrange or delete comments. Don't split a backend into
  `fs.go` + `object.go` — keep it in `remote.go`. Put API request/response types
  in a separate `api/types.go`.
- **Use rclone's HTTP stack.** For HTTP backends use the client/transport from
  `fs/fshttp` and (for REST) `lib/rest` — this gives `--dump bodies`,
  `--tpslimit`, `--user-agent`, pacing, etc. for free. Only use a vendor SDK if
  it's genuinely better.
- **Commit messages:** first line is `directory: short user-facing summary`
  (e.g. `drive: add team drive support`); this line feeds the changelog. Add a
  blank line then a body explaining *why*. Reference issues with `Fixes #1234`.
- **Dependencies:** add/update with `go get` and commit the resulting `go.mod`
  and `go.sum` in the same commit. `make tidy` runs `go mod tidy`.

## Documentation

- Backend option help lives in the Go source `Help:` fields (first line is a
  single sentence ending in a period, kept under ~80 chars; `Examples:` for
  enumerations). The Markdown under `docs/content` is **autogenerated**
  by `make backenddocs` — do **not** hand-edit autogenerated sections, and do
  **not** commit regenerated docs (a CI check rejects changes there).
- Command flag help lives in the command's `.go` file (e.g. `cmd/ls/ls.go`),
  single sentence, no trailing period.
- Root files `MANUAL.*`, `rclone.1` are autogenerated — never edit by hand.
